analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject. The repeated object marker אֵת identifies whom God remembered: Noah and the animals with him in the ark. God then sends a wind, and the waters subside.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיִּזְכֹּר, the masculine singular verb “he remembered.” God remembered Noah and the animals with him in the ark.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with singular reference.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּזְכֹּר אֱלֹהִים אֶת נֹחַ, “God remembered Noah,” אֶת marks the proper name נֹחַ as the direct object of וַיִּזְכֹּר. The following וְאֵת and וְאֶת introduce the other objects of the same verb.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּזְכֹּר אֱלֹהִים אֶת נֹחַ, “God remembered Noah,” אֶת marks Noah as the direct object. The verse also names the animals with him in the ark, identifying him as the Noah of the flood narrative.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 8:1 as evidence for the existing definite-object sense in et.
draft.definition: Introduces a definite direct object, including a further object coordinated with one already named.
draft.evidence: Genesis 8:1 repeats the marker before each object of “remembered”. At the marked occurrence it introduces כָּל הַחַיָּה.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּזְכֹּר אֱלֹהִים אֶת נֹחַ וְאֵת כָּל הַחַיָּה, God remembered both Noah and all the wild animals. The prefix וְ־ coordinates the second object with Noah, and אֵת marks כָּל הַחַיָּה as a further definite object of וַיִּזְכֹּר. The same construction recurs before כָּל הַבְּהֵמָה.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed coordinating conjunction וְ־ “and” + unsuffixed definite direct-object marker אֵת.

analysis.evidence: In וְאֵת כָּל הַחַיָּה, כָּל modifies the definite collective noun הַחַיָּה. God remembered all the wild animals with Noah in the ark, alongside the livestock named in the parallel phrase וְאֶת כָּל הַבְּהֵמָה.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The verse pairs כָּל הַחַיָּה, “all the wild animals,” with כָּל הַבְּהֵמָה, “all the livestock,” naming two groups aboard the ark with Noah.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ־ prefixes a feminine singular absolute noun used collectively.
analysis.sense: wild beast, beast of the field

draft.change: Add Genesis 8:1 as an example of the existing definite-object sense.
draft.definition: Introduces a definite noun phrase as the direct object of a verb.
draft.evidence: Genesis 8:1 repeats אֵת before each of the three objects of “remembered.” Its third occurrence introduces all the livestock.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 8:1, וְאֶת introduces כָּל הַבְּהֵמָה, “all the livestock,” as the third object of וַיִּזְכֹּר, “he remembered.” The repeated particle marks each object in turn, and the prefixed וְ joins the livestock to the list.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to the unsuffixed direct-object particle אֶת.

analysis.evidence: In וְאֶת כָּל הַבְּהֵמָה, כָּל stands in construct with the definite collective noun הַבְּהֵמָה. God remembered all the livestock with Noah in the ark, in parallel with כָּל הַחַיָּה, “all the wild animals.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The verse lists כָּל הַחַיָּה and כָּל הַבְּהֵמָה as distinct groups with Noah in the ark. Paired with the wild animals, הַבְּהֵמָה denotes the livestock collectively.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces the relative clause אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ בַּתֵּבָה, “that were with him in the ark,” describing the animals mentioned immediately before it.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add תֵּבָה under its own consonants, תבה. The verse gives no basis for assigning the noun to תאר.
draft.definition: A container made to keep its occupants safe on water. In Genesis it is Noah’s ark.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:17–18 describes the waters lifting the ark, and Genesis 8:1 places the animals inside it with Noah. Exodus 2:3 uses the same noun for the papyrus basket in which Moses’ mother placed him.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ בַּתֵּבָה means ‘that were with him in the ark.’ The suffix on אִתּוֹ refers to Noah, and בַּתֵּבָה identifies where the animals were with him.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with prefixed בְּ ‘in’ and the definite article הַ־, together realized as בַּ־ with doubling of the following ת.
analysis.sense: The ark that carried Noah and the animals on the floodwaters.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject, רוּחַ is the wind that God causes to move, and עַל הָאָרֶץ specifies its path over the earth.
analysis.gloss: and he made a wind pass over
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיַּעֲבֵר. The same God who remembered Noah now caused a wind to pass over the earth.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with singular verbal agreement.

analysis.evidence: רוּחַ is the object of וַיַּעֲבֵר. God caused a wind to pass over the earth (עַל הָאָרֶץ), and the waters subsided (וַיָּשֹׁכּוּ הַמָּיִם).
analysis.morphology: Common noun of common gender, singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּעֲבֵר אֱלֹהִים רוּחַ עַל הָאָרֶץ, God causes a wind to pass over the earth. The phrase עַל הָאָרֶץ describes the wind’s path.
In רוּחַ עַל הָאָרֶץ, the earth is the expanse over which God sends the wind as the floodwaters subside.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a singular absolute common noun of common gender.

draft.change: Add the Hebrew verb שָׁכַךְ with its intransitive Qal sense in Gen.8.1.
draft.evidence: In Gen.8.1, וַיָּשֹׁכּוּ הַמָּיִם means “and the waters subsided” after God sent a wind over the earth.

analysis.evidence: The plural subject הַמָּיִם follows וַיָּשֹׁכּוּ. After God causes a wind to pass over the earth, the verse reports what the waters do: they subside.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third masculine plural, with prefixed וַ־ and plural ending ־וּ.

draft.change: Add Genesis 8:1 as evidence for the existing sense “a body or flow of water.”
draft.definition: Here מַיִם denotes the floodwaters covering the land.
draft.evidence: Genesis 8:1 describes the same waters that rose in Genesis 7:18–20, now subsiding as a wind passes over the earth.

analysis.evidence: After God sends a wind over the earth, וַיָּשֹׁכּוּ הַמָּיִם says that the waters subsided. The definite noun is the subject of the plural verb and refers to the floodwaters surrounding Noah’s ark.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ with doubling of the initial מ, followed by a masculine plural noun in the absolute state. The verse-final form מָּיִם has pausal lengthening.
analysis.sense: a body or flow of water
